sections.h2: How should I decide how to sell a house in Issaquah?
sections.html:
Start with the two facts that drive every sale: how fast you need the money and how much work the house needs. With a Census median home value of $963,000 in Issaquah, a few percentage points on price are large dollar amounts, so the comparison between routes deserves a real spreadsheet.

  • Traditional listing: The widest buyer pool, and the longest runway. Plan for prep work, showings, a buyer's inspection and financing contingencies.
  • Sale without an agent: You handle pricing, photographs, the purchase contract and the disclosure form yourself.
  • Direct purchase for cash: No loan approval stands between you and closing. Ask for the price, the closing date and the costs you will pay in one written offer, then put that net figure beside your other options.

sections.h2: What sets Issaquah apart from the other Eastside suburbs?
sections.html:
Issaquah lies about 15 miles east-southeast of Seattle at the south end of Lake Sammamish, inside 11.40 square miles. Interstate 90 cuts through the valley. Bellevue is the neighbor to the west and Sammamish to the north, and the city sits inside the Mountains to Sound Greenway.

Three small mountains known as the Issaquah Alps frame the city: Cougar Mountain to the west, Squak Mountain to the south and Tiger Mountain to the southeast. Most of that land is public, as Squak Mountain State Park, Cougar Mountain Regional Wildland Park, West Tiger Mountain Natural Resources Conservation Area and Tiger Mountain State Forest. Sizable neighborhoods sit on the lower slopes of Cougar and Squak. Winters are chilly and very wet, while summers are warm and moderately humid, and winter rainfall runs many times the summer amount.

The area was called Squak Valley before it was Issaquah, a name drawn from a Lushootseed word. The city was incorporated on April 29, 1892, started as a coal mining town and then turned to lumber. Boeing supplied most local jobs through much of the twentieth century. Costco moved its global headquarters to Issaquah in June 1996, and Microsoft, Siemens Medical Solutions, Darigold, SanMar and Boehm's Candies are also named among local employers. The Issaquah Salmon Hatchery, built in 1936, is the most visited hatchery in Washington, and Salmon Days brings crowds to town in early October.

One local project may change the map near downtown: a gravel quarry operated by Lakeside Industries on 120 acres just north of the historic center is planned to become a residential and commercial neighborhood over a 30-year period as quarrying winds down.

sections.h2: What must I tell a buyer about my Issaquah house?
sections.html:
Washington's RCW 64.06.020 requires the seller of improved residential property to hand the buyer a completed disclosure statement, unless the buyer has waived it or the transfer is exempt. Delivery is due within five business days after both sides sign a written purchase contract, unless they agree otherwise. The buyer then has three business days to rescind.

The form asks questions you can answer ahead of time. The title section covers legal authority to sell, first rights of refusal, options, leases and rental agreements, life estates, and encroachments or boundary disputes. Gather your deed, any lease, survey and permit records before listing, because a rushed form invites follow-up questions and delay.

sections.h2: Do state housing laws let a buyer add units on an Issaquah lot?
sections.html:
Issaquah updated its code to meet state laws that require middle housing and at least two accessory dwelling units per lot, so ask the city what your lot allows. State law (HB 1110 from 2023) requires cities to allow middle housing such as duplexes and townhouses in areas of mostly detached homes, with rules due by June 30, 2025. HB 1337 requires cities to allow at least two accessory dwelling units on a lot in addition to the main home. The city's schedule for the update lists tentative City Council adoption on May 19, 2025, along with ordinances for middle housing, ADUs, parking and street standards.

  • Permits: Register at MyBuildingPermit.com to submit most permits.
  • Questions: Community Planning and Development answers at CPD@issaquahwa.gov or 425-837-3100, and offers online meetings with staff.
  • Larger projects: The city encourages a pre-application meeting.

If you are selling a house with a basement apartment, a detached unit or plans on file, ask the city what permits exist so your buyer does not inherit a problem.

sections.h2: How much excise tax applies to an Issaquah sale?
sections.html:
The Department of Revenue says the real estate excise tax is usually paid by the seller, and the tax is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale. Issaquah is in King County. State tax is graduated: 1.1 percent applies up to $525,000 of the price, and 1.28 percent applies from there up to $1,525,000. A local rate is added, which your escrow officer can calculate.

Because the median home value here is $963,000, the numbers are large. A sale at that price would carry about $11,381 in state tax: $5,775 on the first $525,000 plus about $5,606 on the remaining $438,000. Interest and penalties start if the tax is not paid within one month of the sale. Ask escrow to show the figure on your closing statement before you sign.

sections.h2: How do roads, transit and schools shape buyer interest in Issaquah?
sections.html:
Interstate 90 and State Route 900 serve the city, and Front Street through the historic downtown carries about 20,000 vehicle trips a day, a chronic congestion point. The Issaquah Transit Center has 1,010 park-and-ride spaces and Issaquah Highlands has 819. Metro and Sound Transit Express buses run to Bellevue, Mercer Island, North Bend and Redmond, and a Link light rail line to Issaquah is proposed by 2050. Mean travel time to work is 25.3 minutes.

The Issaquah School District serves about 21,358 students in 28 schools in and around the city, and it extends into southern Sammamish and northern Renton. Swedish Medical Center opened a hospital in Issaquah Highlands in November 2011.

sections.h2: What should I confirm before accepting an offer on my Issaquah house?
sections.html:
• Read the offer for the closing date, the price and each cost assigned to you.
  • Order a payoff figure from your lender so the net amount is exact.
  • Ask the buyer how funds will be shown and whether any inspection or repair demand is attached.
  • Pull your permit history from Community Planning and Development, especially for a finished basement, a deck or a detached unit.
  • Have escrow estimate the state and local excise tax before you agree to a price.

faqs.q: Can I add a backyard cottage to my Issaquah property before selling?
faqs.a: Possibly. Under HB 1337 cities must allow at least two accessory dwelling units per lot, and Issaquah updated its code accordingly. Contact Community Planning and Development at 425-837-3100 before you plan any building work.

faqs.q: How soon must I give the buyer a seller disclosure statement?
faqs.a: Within five business days after the written contract is accepted, unless the parties agree otherwise. RCW 64.06.020 gives the buyer three business days after delivery to rescind, and the buyer may waive the statement, or the transfer may be exempt.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for a building permit in Issaquah?
faqs.a: Register at MyBuildingPermit.com to submit most permits. For questions, contact Community Planning and Development at CPD@issaquahwa.gov or 425-837-3100, and ask about an online meeting with staff or a pre-application meeting for larger projects.

The Issaquah School District, which runs 28 schools for roughly 21,358 students. Its boundaries include the southern part of Sammamish with zip code 98075 and the northern part of Renton, so check the district for your exact address.

faqs.q: How far is Issaquah from Seattle, and how do I get there?
faqs.a: About 15 miles east-southeast of Seattle, along Interstate 90. Metro and Sound Transit Express buses connect Issaquah to Bellevue and Mercer Island, where riders can reach the Link 2 Line.
